references.text: The Lord explains that Moses is to speak to Aaron, and Aaron is to speak to the people on Moses' behalf, as a parallel to how Moses is to command and Aaron is to speak to Pharaoh.
Moses is told to say everything the Lord commands him to Pharaoh, but Moses objects that he has uncircumcised lips.
The context where the Lord says Moses will be like God to Pharaoh, and Aaron will be his prophet.
The Lord tells Moses that he is to perform all the signs before Pharaoh, but Pharaoh will not let the people go.
Moses' original calling to lead the children of Israel out of Egypt, which is the ultimate goal of the message to Pharaoh.
Moses and Aaron go to Pharaoh and ask him to let the people of Israel go, but Pharaoh refuses.
The promise of a prophet like Moses who will speak what God commands, a prophetic role that Aaron here fills in relation to Moses.
Jeremiah is told to go to everyone he is sent to and say everything the Lord commands him, parallel to Moses' mission.
Direct narrative connection where 6:11 introduces the mission that 7:2 details with the division of roles between Moses and Aaron.
6:13 summarizes the common command that 7:2 operationalizes with specific roles for Moses and Aaron.
6:27 identifies Moses and Aaron as the central actors in the confrontation instructed in 7:2.
4:22 delivers the theological content of the message that 7:2 commands Moses and Aaron to convey to Pharaoh.
